text.en: A river changes as it travels from a sparkling stream to the wide sea.

The poet addresses the river directly. At first it is little and bright, dancing over yellow pebbles like a child at play. Then it swells and rushes on like impetuous youth. Later it is broad, deep and still as time, and at last it dashes headlong into the sea, which the poem compares to eternity.
The river's journey is compared to human life: childhood, youth, maturity and the end. The poem uses personification and similes to make the river seem alive.
Notice the repeated address River, river and the similes beginning with like. Learn the words foliage, impetuous, brimming and eternity.
